trigger: Night. Home. After the pharmacy. Chapter end.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Candles. Windows open for any breeze. Carly reading your dead phone like it might change its mind.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: It still has the voicemail. From Sunday. You never listened to it.

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: Braith. It's Dad. Sky's doing something crazy out here. Green, all the way down to Walker Lake.

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: Radio says the grid's going. Not just us. Everywhere. Listen. Come home, both of you, before—

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The message ends. Three seconds of silence. Then the phone dies for good.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: Seventy miles. You could make it on what we've got.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: You kept the gas for this. I saw. It's okay. I'd have done the same.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: Well. Maybe not on what we've got.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: I'm not leaving. People are still walking into dispatch. Somebody has to write it down.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: I know. So go. I mean it. I'll be here.

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: Don't promise me soon. Nobody gets soon anymore.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Wraith climbs onto the bed, which is not allowed, and nobody says anything.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Somewhere east, your father is waiting by a phone that will never ring.
